reviewer: Codex visual inspection of actual captured images
identity_verification: Selected source-frame identities match completed runner output bindings; actual current raw CSV/check records, all 50 sheets, all 38 inspected originals, engine log, and fresh-build record hashes match their bindings. Runtime binaries were not rehashed by this visual review.

inspection.method: Static chronological contact sheets at native crop scale, plus original full 1600x900 JPEGs displayed through view_image. All 33 windows and all 50 pages were inspected, each page left-to-right then top-to-bottom in source-frame order. Windows were processed by earliest selected frame; overlapping pump/near windows were inspected separately. Full frames supplied composition, crop-edge and endpoint context.

overall_findings: All six variants retain coherent weapon and hand orientation through the selected near-cursor arcs. No visible arm inversion, reversed barrel, detached grip or missing held weapon was found in those sampled windows.

Pistol/rifle magazines visibly leave the weapon and fall separately. The two shotguns show support-hand/fore-end pump recovery and shell-loading hand sequences. Small slide, bolt and shell-port details remain limited by the camera scale and occlusion.

Three machine handoffs show weapon travel toward the tray; separate full-frame endpoints show the transferred weapon in the tray and the other slot in hand. All three retrieval windows show the weapon coming from the tray into a normal firing grip.
Cyan, purple and amber upgrade identities remain distinguishable in these reviewed weapon samples. This is not a complete UI or aura comparison review.
limitations: This is inspection of static chronological captured frames, not continuous video playback or a perceptual smoothness/framerate test. Captured JPEGs do not contain every rendered frame.

The 33 windows cover selected near-aim, mechanical and transfer intervals, not the entire 5257-frame presentation, all possible directions, every reload cycle, live enemy reactions, or full UI/aura coverage.

Top-down camera scale and hand overlap prevent independent certification of fine pistol-slide travel, rifle-bolt travel and exact shell-to-loading-port contact. The broad hand motions and visible separate parts are described only where seen.

Some near-aim intervals do not retain a muzzle flash even though they are anchored to actual shot-counter events. This review does not infer unobserved flashes or use screenshots to prove cadence/latency.

Several left-facing long-weapon crops truncate the far barrel/tracer edge. Original full frames were inspected for that context. Three default handoff windows end during transfer; four additional endpoint originals establish subsequent tray state, not every intervening frame.

Production PlayerController key dispatch and projected cursor were scripted; sandbox controls and the final fatal-damage fixture are disclosed in capture checks. No native human input, survival run, audio audition, mouse-to-photon latency, performance isolation or complete publication approval is claimed.
The final source commit and packaged run are bound to completed session/build records. This review compared artifacts to those records but did not rehash runtime binaries itself.

windows.name: M1911_near_8cm
windows.finding: Both hands remain on the pistol grip as the torso and planted stance turn left through the close-cursor sample; the captured flash/tracer starts at the forward pistol end. No backward-facing weapon or arm inversion is visible.

windows.name: M1911_near_35cm
windows.finding: The pistol and joined grip sweep smoothly across the left side of the torso in the seven captured frames; the cursor remains near the muzzle. This particular window does not visibly retain a muzzle flash.

windows.name: M1911_near_95cm
windows.finding: The downward-facing shot shows flash/tracer ahead of the pistol, followed by a coherent leftward turn with the grip and elbows retained.

windows.name: pistol_magdrop
windows.finding: The supporting hand leaves the grip and a separate dark magazine drops beside the player, descending across successive frames before settling on the floor. The weapon remains in the shooting hand.

windows.name: pistol_magin_slide
windows.finding: The supporting hand returns beneath and beside the raised pistol, then both arms extend back to the firing grip. The spent magazine stays on the floor. The full frame shows 7/49 ammo during the late reload; individual slide travel is too small and partly overlapped by the hand to certify from these pixels alone.
windows.limitation: Magazine insertion/slide completion is not a pixel-level dimensional check; this camera shows the broad hand sequence, while fine slide motion remains unresolved.

windows.name: M4A1_near_8cm
windows.finding: Rifle remains shouldered with the support hand under the fore-end during the close leftward sweep. The barrel/tracer reaches the crop edge beside the Mystery Box; full frames are required for that boundary context. Original frame_00880 confirms the complete forward muzzle and tracer beyond the sheet boundary; the weapon silhouette itself is not missing.
windows.limitation: The leftmost muzzle/tracer vicinity meets the default crop edge.

windows.name: M4A1_near_35cm
windows.finding: A captured shot flashes at the front of the rifle while the support hand stays beneath the fore-end. Subsequent frames turn the whole held rifle across the left-facing arc without a visible reversal.

windows.name: M4A1_near_95cm
windows.finding: The downward-facing captured shot and subsequent left turn retain the rifle stock, trigger hand and supporting arm relationship. The barrel moves coherently with the torso.

windows.name: rifle_magdrop
windows.finding: A separate rifle magazine visibly leaves the well near frame_01032 and falls beside the player through frame_01040. The support arm drops away while the shooting hand keeps the rifle raised.

windows.name: rifle_magin_bolt
windows.finding: The support hand rises to the magazine well, leaves a seated magazine visible beneath the rifle, then moves along the receiver area and returns to the fore-end. The old magazine remains separate on the floor. Original frame_01063 shows 24/185 while the reload is still finishing.
windows.limitation: The receiver-level hand action is visible, but individual bolt travel is too small/dark to certify independently at this camera scale.

windows.name: rifle_handoff
windows.finding: The character presents the rifle toward the tray, and the gun visibly rotates/translates away from its firing orientation as the machine changes from amber to cyan. The default interval ends during the transfer. Extra originals frame_01445 and frame_01450 show the rifle resting inside the cyan tray while the character has switched to the other pistol and moved away.
windows.limitation: Final tray settling occurs after the default crop interval; extra original-frame context is inspected separately.

windows.name: rifle_retrieval
windows.finding: The rifle rises from the tray into the extended hands, then returns to a normal shouldered grip. The full frame identifies the retrieved Overcurrent and 36/540 ammo; the machine changes back to amber after retrieval.

windows.name: Overcurrent_near_8cm
windows.finding: The upgraded rifle retains a coherent shoulder/fore-end grip through the near-cursor sweep. Cyan receiver accents remain visible between shots. The leftmost barrel is close to the crop edge; the full-frame view confirms its forward orientation.

windows.name: Overcurrent_near_35cm
windows.finding: The rifle follows the close cursor through a left-facing arc with the support hand staying beneath it. Cyan material detail is visible without a captured flash in this interval.

windows.name: Overcurrent_near_95cm
windows.finding: The upgraded rifle stays aligned with both hands as it turns from downward to leftward aim; cyan receiver treatment remains visible. No reversed barrel or elbow flip is visible in these seven frames.
windows.limitation: No muzzle flash is retained in this selected captured-frame interval; shot timing is assessed in separate telemetry.

windows.name: pistol_handoff
windows.finding: The pistol is extended toward the tray, then leaves the hands as cyan processing begins. Near the end, the other-slot rifle appears in the player's hands while the small pistol moves toward the tray. Original frame_02561 shows the pistol separately inside the cyan tray and Overcurrent in the character's hands.
windows.limitation: Final tray settling is outside the default interval; an additional original is inspected for that endpoint.

windows.name: pistol_retrieval
windows.finding: The purple pistol moves out of the tray into the extended hands, then the arms return to the normal two-hand pistol pose. The full frame identifies Last Word with 14/168 ammo. Its purple effect is concentrated on the weapon.

windows.name: LastWord_near_8cm
windows.finding: The purple pistol and joined hands sweep left around the close cursor without reversing the gun or turning either arm inside out. A purple shot effect appears ahead of the barrel in the first selected frame.

windows.name: LastWord_near_35cm
windows.finding: The purple pistol tracks the cursor near the body with a stable two-hand grip and a consistent turning stance; no arm/weapon flip is visible.

windows.name: LastWord_near_95cm
windows.finding: A purple muzzle flash and forward tracer are visible during the downward-facing shot, followed by a coherent leftward turn. The effect lights the front of the torso transiently while the weapon remains identifiable.

windows.name: lastword_magdrop
windows.finding: The supporting hand releases the purple pistol grip and a separate dark magazine descends beside the character through the later frames. The weapon stays raised in the shooting hand; the nearby tray does not conceal the drop.

windows.name: 870_pump
windows.finding: After the visible shot, the support hand and brown fore-end draw back toward the receiver and return forward as the character keeps turning. A small red/brown ejected shell travels to the player's right in the second page. The stock stays at the shoulder.
windows.limitation: Pump action overlaps a body turn, so these static frames support the visible sequence, not a continuous smoothness judgment.

windows.name: 870_near_8cm
windows.finding: The long shotgun stays shouldered and both arms keep a coherent grip during the near-cursor leftward sweep. The default crop cuts the far barrel end in several frames; original frame_03607 shows its full continuation beside the Mystery Box.
windows.limitation: Muzzle-edge context comes from the original full frame; no retained flash is claimed for this interval.

windows.name: 870_near_35cm
windows.finding: The captured flash and pellet traces emerge ahead of the long barrel; the support hand stays on the fore-end as the body rotates left. The crop boundary cuts the far tracer, while the original confirms the complete gun silhouette.

windows.name: 870_near_95cm
windows.finding: A downward-facing shot is followed by a coherent leftward sweep, with the stock and both hands retained. The original shows the empty 0/36 state after this last-shell shot.

windows.name: 870_shell
windows.finding: The left hand reaches from the body toward the underside of the receiver, with a small red shell visible at the hand in portions of the approach; it returns and begins another insertion. The original shows 2/34 during the continuing reload.
windows.limitation: The shell and loading-port contact occupy only a few native pixels and are partly overlapped by the hand; precise penetration/contact cannot be measured visually.

windows.name: shotgun_handoff
windows.finding: The long shotgun is presented into the tray, then rotates visibly away from the hands as cyan processing starts. The other-slot purple pistol becomes visible near the transfer end. Original frame_04120 shows the shotgun fully inside the cyan tray while the character holds Last Word and retreats.
windows.limitation: The default interval ends just before full tray settling; an extra original is inspected for the endpoint.

windows.name: shotgun_retrieval
windows.finding: The amber upgraded shotgun rises from its vertical tray orientation toward the hands, then settles into a shoulder/fore-end grip. The full frame identifies Gravebreaker at 8/120; the tray becomes empty and returns to amber.

windows.name: gravebreaker_pump
windows.finding: The amber shotgun's visible shot is followed by the supporting hand drawing toward the receiver and returning forward while the character turns. A small ejected shell moves rightward across subsequent frames. The upgraded receiver remains distinguishable.

windows.name: Gravebreaker_near_8cm
windows.finding: The selected close-cursor interval overlaps the first pump recovery: the barrel turns from right toward downward, with the stock, trigger hand and supporting arm keeping a coherent relationship. No arm inversion or reversed weapon appears.
windows.limitation: This event-anchored window follows the flash; its first seven frames are also present in the longer pump window.

windows.name: Gravebreaker_near_35cm
windows.finding: An amber shot effect and traces appear ahead of the barrel as the upgraded shotgun turns left. Both hands retain their relationship to the stock and fore-end; the barrel crosses the default crop boundary near the end and is visible in full-frame context.

windows.name: Gravebreaker_near_95cm
windows.finding: The downward shot emits amber traces from the front of the weapon, followed by a controlled leftward turn. The receiver's amber identity remains visible and no arm or barrel reversal appears.

windows.name: gravebreaker_shell
windows.finding: The support hand moves from the body to the underside of the raised receiver and back, with the small red shell visible during portions of the approach. The gun remains supported by the shooting hand and shoulder.
windows.limitation: The fine shell-to-port contact is partly hidden by the hand and cannot be certified from this top-down camera; the sample does not alone establish a full ammunition cycle.
